title: dedicated-fleet-autoscaler-throughput-guarantees-burst-controls-and-util-reporting-refactor
author: Ravi Patel
description: Motivation: Customers on Redwood Dedicated requested stronger throughput guarantees during short bursts while preserving utilization accuracy for billing/observability. The previous autoscaler frequently over-allocated during transient spikes and under-reported burst consumption, which caused cost surprises for customers using reserved pools. This PR implements a combined approach: (1) a token-bucket based burst allowance per fleet with configurable smoothing, (2) a fast-path throughput guarantee that pre-allocates capacity for critical routes within a bounded time window, and (3) a refactor of the utilization reporting pipeline to emit stable, debounced metrics that account for token-bucket usage and pre-allocated throughput. Summary of changes: - autoscaler/core: introduce token_bucket_manager (configurable burst_size, refill_rate, smoothing_window) and integrate into allocation decision path. - autoscaler/policy: new ThroughputGuaranteePolicy that reserves ephemeral slots for routes marked critical; supports soft/hard guarantees and fallback to compatible model variants. - metrics/reporting: refactor utilization aggregator to include burst_consumed and guarantee_reserved tags; add debouncing to reduce noisy spikes in the per-fleet reported utilization. - api: expose new fleet settings (burst_allowance, guarantee_ttl, smoothing_window) in Dedicated fleet API and console. - docs: update dedicated autoscaling and pricing docs to clarify how burst allowances are applied and how utilization is reported for billing. - tests: add unit + integration tests that simulate burst scenarios, and an end-to-end canary that runs against a staging dedicated fleet. Checklist: - [x] Implement token bucket manager and integrate with autoscaler decision path - [x] Add ThroughputGuaranteePolicy with configurable parameters - [x] Refactor utilization reporting pipeline and add metrics/tags - [x] Add API surface and console toggle behind feature flag - [x] Tests for unit, integration, and canary - [x] Update docs and release notes Backwards compatibility: New fleet settings default to conservative values (burst_allowance=0, guarantee_ttl=0) so existing fleets are unchanged unless explicitly migrated. Migration notes: If customers opt-in to guarantees we record a migration event and emit a one-time billing-preview metric to help forecasting. Related work: ENG-1223 (autoscaler refactor), ENG-1307 (billing/usage reporting), SUP-4532 (customer report of cost spikes).

release_notes: Added per-fleet burst allowances (token-bucket) and throughput guarantees with configurable TTL; utilization reporting now includes burst_consumed and guarantee_reserved tags. Defaults are conservative; opt-in required for guarantees.
notes: This PR stabilizes observed billing spikes for a set of enterprise customers by ensuring bursts are bounded and visible in utilization metrics.
